picked.t: Danish footwear company shuts Vietnam factory, 1,600 workers lose jobs
picked.body: The closure will affect more than 1,600 workers. Truong Van Phong, deputy head of the Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing and Industrial Zones Authority (Hepza), said Tuesday that ECCO Sko A/S of Denmark, the sole owner of ECCO Vietnam Co., Ltd., had decided to dissolve the company. The company attributed the decision to years of declining market demand, which had resulted in excess production capacity. The factory closure is part of the group's global manufacturing restructuring plan, which aims to consolidate operations at a smaller number of its facilities. Employment contracts for workers not offered continued employment will end on Nov. 30, or earlier if their contracts expire before that date. Some employees will be retained for a few months to assist with the dissolution process. The company has promised to pay all outstanding wages, compensation for unused annual leave, and other amounts owed in accordance with regulations. In addition to statutory severance allowances, it will also pay half a month's base salary for each year of service. Any period of employment shorter than 12 months will be rounded up to one year. Workers will also receive a 13th-month salary proportionate to the time they worked during the year. Those asked to assist with the dissolution will receive an additional bonus equivalent to 50% of one day's base salary for each day worked. ECCO Vietnam has also pledged to complete the confirmation of employees' social insurance contribution records and return relevant documents to them. Phong said the company had not defaulted on social insurance premiums. On Monday afternoon, Hepza, the Ho Chi Minh City Labor Federation, and local authorities met with company officials and told them to fulfill all commitments regarding workers' benefits and facilitate their hiring by other businesses. Phong said at least eight nearby companies had expressed interest in hiring around 1,611 workers as of Monday. He add that Hepza, trade unions, and local authorities would coordinate efforts to put affected employees onto new job opportunities. Phung Thai Quang, deputy chairman of the Ho Chi Minh City Labor Federation, said he had instructed industrial zone and company-level trade unions to review employee lists and provide support to those losing their jobs. The city's Trade Union Labor Consultation and Support Center will review the policies announced by ECCO Vietnam, compare them with legal requirements, and monitor their implementation. ECCO is a Danish footwear brand founded in 1963. Its factory in the Bau Bang Industrial Park in former Binh Duong Province began operations in April 2020. The 12-hectare plant cost VND861 billion (US$34 million) and had an annual capacity of 8.1 million footwear products and parts. The dissolution of ECCO Vietnam comes even as recruitment opportunities in the footwear industry remain limited. According to the Ho Chi Minh City Employment Service Center, the garment and textile and footwear sectors had 1,306 vacancies but 2,473 applicants in October.

picked.t: 베트남, 내년도 지역별 최저임금 평균 7.8% 인상…정부 시행령
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남의 최저임금이 내년 1월부터 현재와 비교해 평균 7.8% 인상된다. 베트남 정부는 최근 2027년도 지역별 월 최저임금을 규정한 시행령 제399/2026/ND-CP호를 공포했다. 이에 따라 근로계약을 체결한 근로자들의 지역별 최저임금은 월 404만~570만 동으로 현재보다 31만~39만 동, 평균 7.8% 인상된다. 시행령에 따르면, 내년 1월부터 적용될 지역별 최저임금은 △1급지 월 570만 동(221달러), +39만 동(15달러, 7.3%) △2급지 월 508만 동(197달러), +35만 동(14달러, 7.4%) △3급지 445만 동(172달러), +31만 동(12달러, 7.5%) △4급지 404만 동(157달러), +34만 동(13달러, 9.2%) 등이다. 지역별 최저시급 또한 △1급지 2만7,400동(1.1달러) △2급지 2만4,400동(95센트) △3급지 2만1,400동(83센트) △4급지 1만9,400동(75센트) 등으로 인상된다. 규정에 따라 사용자는 사업장이 속한 지역의 최저임금을 적용해야 한다. 여러 지역에 사업장을 둔 기업은 해당 사업장이 소재한 지역의 최저임금을 적용한다. 이 밖에도 산업단지나 수출가공단지, 디지털기술집중구역, 특별경제구역, 자유무역지대 또는 첨단기술농업단지 등 최저임금이 서로 다른 지역에 걸쳐있는 지역들의 경우, 해당 지역들 중 가장 높은 최저임금이 적용된다. 지역명이 변경되거나 분할되는 경우, 새 규정 발표전까지 이전 지역의 최저임금이 적용되며, 서로 다른 지역이 합병돼 새 지역이 생길 경우, 가장 높은 수준의 최저임금이 적용된다.

picked.t: Vietnam, Japan's biggest source of foreign workers, struggles to recruit more
picked.body: Recruiters blame a weaker yen and more jobs at home, and many workers are turning to other markets, especially Taiwan, where the wait to depart is shorter. For almost a year, Pham Van Trong, human resources manager at a company that supplies workers to Japan and Taiwan, has traveled to rural and mountainous northern Vietnam twice a month to recruit young people for jobs abroad. Based in An Khanh, Hanoi, the company has sent workers to Japan for more than 10 years in food processing, mechanical engineering, automobiles, machine building, seafood and agriculture, and to Taiwan for electronics work. It asks local Women's Union and Youth Union officials to help find candidates, but they turn up only about 10% of the workers it needs. "The villages are empty of young people because they've moved to the big cities to work in services, drive for ride-hailing apps or take factory jobs. Visit their homes and you only find old people and small children," he said. Japan is one of Vietnam's three traditional labor markets. Vietnamese were the largest group of foreign workers there as of October 2025, according to Japan's labor ministry. At the end of June, 176,865 Vietnamese were in Japan as technical interns, more than any other nationality, and another 176,915 as specified skilled workers, Immigration Services Agency figures show. Japan took nearly 28,500 Vietnamese workers in the first half of this year, the most of any market but down from 35,240 a year earlier, Vietnam's Ministry of Home Affairs data show. By the end of August, Taiwan had pulled ahead, 39,890 to 35,837. Trong's company takes more than 600 job orders a year from Japanese partners on average, but filling them has become very difficult, with its supply of candidates down about 60% from before. A decade ago, seven or eight applicants competed for each order. Now there are two per position, or the company accepts anyone who turns up. Its recruiters post in online groups and split up to search the provinces. The company has also relaxed its selection criteria to fill more places. In food processing and auto parts manufacturing, for example, workers used to need to be at least 1.65 meters tall and physically fit to cope with the work and winter weather. Now candidates who fall just short of the height and weight requirements still pass. The company provides transport and covers extra costs for trainees during preparation. Some candidates interview before the Lunar New Year, or Tet, and leave after the holiday, but quotas still go unfilled. Trong said several factors were behind the falling supply, among them more jobs at home. Unskilled construction workers, for example, can now earn around VND20 million ($770). But the main reason, he said, is the weaker yen. One yen used to fetch VND200-220 and now fetches about VND160-170, so every 10,000 yen ($64) is worth VND400,000-600,000 ($15-23) less once converted. Workers' total incomes are 1.2 to 1.5 times what they were 10 years ago, but what they can save and send home has not kept pace. On total incomes of VND30-40 million ($1,150-1,540) a month, workers used to send home VND20-25 million ($770-960), and their savings still hover around that level. "With the yen sliding and savings not growing, workers will think twice," Trong said. Long waits add to the pressure. A National Statistics Office survey found that the average migrant worker waits about six months between starting preparations and departing. Japan, with its strict requirements, takes about seven months of preparation, compared with about four for other destinations in Asia. The wait can leave workers without income, raising costs and the risk of debt, as more than half borrow to go abroad. "Japanese is also a barrier for unskilled workers, because both the receiving and sending sides demand a high level. But whether it's Japan or any other market, the more of the language you know, the better," he said. Even for Taiwan, a less demanding market than Japan that draws workers because departure takes only one to two months, the company's supply of workers has fallen about 30%. It receives 300-400 electronics orders a year and meets about 60-70% of demand. Kim Thanh, who asked that her real name not be used, handles recruitment at a company that sends workers to Japan. She said its warehousing and food processing orders for this year are nearly filled, but three mechanical engineering orders for eight workers have gone unfilled since the start of the month. Thanh said generational differences in attitudes to work also make recruiting harder. Workers born in the 1980s and 1990s generally don't mind heavy work, while younger people weigh other things. Food processing and warehousing, known as "light work, high pay" jobs, tend to draw young applicants. Mechanical work such as semi-automatic welding or operating cutting machines is grueling, demands high skill and attracts few takers. Each order used to draw three or four applicants per place. picked.t: Companies look to absorb 1,600 workers laid off after HCMC-based Danish shoe factory closes
picked.body: Representatives of several companies visited the headquarters of ECCO in the Bau Bang Industrial Park on Tuesday to distribute leaflets and apprise workers about job openings. They are looking to hire general workers, technicians, administrative staff, and human resources personnel, with some companies offering immediate employment. Truong Van Phong, deputy head of the Ho Chi Minh City Export Processing and Industrial Zones Authority (Hepza), said at least 12 companies have registered to recruit workers after ECCO Vietnam announced its dissolution. They are in fact seeking to fill more than 5,600 positions. Ampacs International Co. Ltd. Alone needs 2,000 workers, Paihong Vietnam wants 1,000, and Cycletech Vietnam has 700 openings. Diamond Vietnam, Waytex Vietnam International, and Hailex Vietnam Technology are each looking for 300 workers, while T.O.P Outdoor Vina, Kammi Vina, and Arneplant Vietnam each have 200 vacancies. The remaining three companies are Fine Chemical Vietnam, Chervon Vietnam Industrial, and Leeda Vietnam, which need 100-180 candidates. According to publicly available information, Chervon offers general workers VND250,000 (US$9.50) per day (eight hours of working) and VND310,000 for a night shift. Overtime is VND41,000 per hour and the monthly attendance bonus is VND260,000. Some technical and quality control positions are advertised at monthly salaries of VND15-25 million. Ampacs is recruiting material control staff at salaries of VND12-16 million, while some administrative and human resources positions offer VND11-14 million. Paihong is hiring technicians specializing in textile production, dyeing, and quality testing at salaries of VND12-20 million. Hepza has asked ECCO Vietnam to facilitate recruitment activities by other companies at its factory. The city will coordinate with trade unions and local authorities to bring together the ECCO workers with prospective employers. At a meeting on the same morning with officials from Hepza and trade unions and local authorities, ECCO said it would pay the workers full November wages though the factory suspended operations Monday and they are no longer required to work. It will also pay a 13th-month salary and additional compensation equivalent to half a month's basic salary for each year of service. Tran Ngoc Huyen, 30, who has worked at ECCO for five years, said she expects to receive a total of 4.5 months' salary, including 2.5 months of compensation, full November salary, and the 13th-month salary. She has a young child at school in Bau Bang Commune, and so plans to find another job in the same area soon. ECCO, owned by ECCO Sko A/S, used to make footwear and had 1,611 workers, including 259 employed by outsourcing contractors. It blamed the decision to close on economic difficulties, years of declining demand, and excess capacity across its global plants. ECCO Group is restructuring and focusing on expanding production in Denmark and at some other locations.

picked.t: Hanoi airport records strongest growth among Southeast Asia's 10 busiest in October
picked.body: Singapore Changi is the busiest airport in Southeast Asia in October by serving 3.66 million scheduled departing seats, representing a 1.66% increase in capacity year-on-year. Canadian superstar The Weeknd performed two massive shows at Singapore's National Stadium on Oct. 2 and 3, drawing large crowds of foreign fans and partly contributed to the airport's traffic flow. Photo by AFP Bangkok Suvarnabhumi International Airport ranks second with 3.34 million seats, up 3.9%. The airport suffered severe ground-handling staff shortage due to historic flooding in Thailand's capital city from late September to early October that affected thousands of passenger. Photo by Reuters Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport claimed the third place with 3.29 million scheduled seats, an increase of 3.8% year-on-year. The airport expects more traffic in coming months as Malaysia-based AirBorneo Airways has opened ticket sales for direct flights between Kuching and Jakarta, with services set to begin on Nov. 13, 2026. The airline said in a statement on Oct. 31 that flights to Soekarno-Hatta International Airport would operate three times a week, on Mondays, Fridays and Sundays. Photo by Reuters Kuala Lumpur International Airport in Malaysia, the largest in Southeast Asia by area, ranks fourth with seat capacity of 3.22 million, down 5.2% year on year. The airport recently began deploying sniffer dogs in departure and arrival halls, as well as baggage-sorting facilities to strengthen security in both passenger areas and airport operational zones, The Star newspaper reported. The sniffer dogs will be stationed at check-in areas to help detect prohibited items early and identify potential security threats linked to targeted flights, New Straits Times reported. Photo by Reuters Ninoy Aquino International Airport ranks fifth with 2.66 million passengers, marking a 1.6% decrease. Located between the cities of Pasay and Parañaque, about 7 kilometers south of Manila, it serves as the primary gateway for travelers to the country. Photo by Reuters Tan Son Nhat Airport in Ho Chi Minh City ranks sixth with 2.29 million passengers, marking a 6.7% increase. The airport handled over 42.4 million passengers last year, a 6.3% year-on-year increase, including 17.8 million international travelers. In recent years, the airport has upgraded infrastructure and improved service quality. From mid-April, the airport has implemented pre-entry information declarations for international arrivals in an effort to reduce immigration processing time. Photo by Quynh Tran Noi Bai International Airport in Hanoi ranked seventh with 1.94 million departing seats, up 14.9% from a year earlier, the fastest growth among the airports listed. The increase came in the same month as Hanoi hosted a two-day concert by South Korean group BigBang. The concerts drew nearly 220,000 visitors to Hanoi, including 68,000 foreigners, generating an estimated VND750 billion (US$29 million) in tourism revenue, according to local authorities. Photo by Giang Huy Thailand's Don Mueang International Airport ranked eighth with 1.56 million departing seats, down 11.2% year on year, the steepest decline among the airports listed. Bangkok's second-largest airport experienced disruptions, flight delays and cancellations in late September and early October due to heavy rain and severe flooding in the city. It started replacing handheld metal-detector checks with manual pat-down searches from Nov. 1, potentially extending security screening times for departing passengers. Photo by Reuters I Gusti Ngurah Rai Airport serving Bali, 13 km south of Denpasar in Tuban, comes in ninth with 1.3 million seats, down 0.9%. As Indonesia's second busiest airport, it acts as a hub for major carriers, offering duty-free shopping, lounges, and close access to Kuta and Jimbaran. Photo by Skytrax Sultan Hasanuddin Airport serving Makassar, the capital of the Indonesian province of South Sulawesi, finishes the top 10 with 960,000 seats, up 4.9% This airport serves as the main gateway to eastern Indonesia and is a major regional aviation hub. It is the largest airport in eastern Indonesia and one of only three international airports in Sulawesi. Photo courtesy of the airport

picked.t: HCMC to build 2 pedestrian bridges over busy downtown street to Saigon River park
picked.body: The two bridges will connect with the pedestrian bridge being built across the Saigon River, and which is expected to open in February next year. The city People's Committee has given in-principle approval for building the two. Both will have steel structures, measure six meters in width, and have elevators and decorative lighting. One will go up to the intersection of Nguyen Hue and Ton Duc Thang, and the other to the intersection of Thai Van Lung Street and Ton Duc Thang. They will allow people visiting the riverside to cross busy Ton Duc Thang Street safely. HCMC Department of Construction is now seeking feedback from relevant agencies before negotiating with the developer. Great Wealth Trading and Services Co. Ltd. will invest in the project under a build-transfer contract. The company will cover all costs related to construction, management, and operation and in return will be allowed to install billboards and LED screens for political communication and advertising and offer services at certain designated places. The company will also renovate piers B and C at the Ba Son area. The former will see repairs, cleaning, and the installation of fences, railings, and access ramps. The riverside area will be landscaped with decorative features and equipped with electricity, water, lighting, security cameras, greenery, and visitor amenities. Pier C will be transformed into a landscaped area with flower gardens and green spaces. The two bridges were originally scheduled for completion by April 30 this year, but the construction was postponed for some procedures to be completed. Nguyen Hue Plaza, 670 m long in the middle of the walking street, opened in 2015 and attracts thousands of visitors daily besides serving as a venue for major events. Thai Van Lung Street is also being studied for redevelopment as a model street promoting traffic culture and "civilized urban living." The 720-meter pedestrian bridge stretching from Bach Dang Wharf Park across the Saigon River to Thu Thiem was connected last month, linking the city center with the new urban area. The VND1 trillion bridge is also funded by a private company.

picked.t: Vietnam posts back-to-back monthly trade surpluses
picked.body: Total import-export turnover in October reached an estimated $122.03 billion, up 3.7% from the previous month and 47.4% year on year, according to the National Statistics Office's socio-economic report released on Tuesday. Exports during the month amounted to $64.67 billion, up 8.7% month-on-month and 51.4% year-on-year, while imports in totaled $57.36 billion, down 1.4% month-on-month but up 43.1% from a year ago. Over the first 10 months of this year, total trade turnover reached $1.01 trillion, up 32.3% year on year, exceeding the $1-trillion mark for the first time. Exports rose 27.5% while imports increased 37.4%, resulting in a trade deficit of $12.07 billion. Exports in the 10-month period amounted to $499.24 billion, with domestic businesses contributing $93.93 billion, up 8.2%, and foreign-invested enterprises $405.31 billion, up 33%. Some 37 export products generated over $1 billion each, accounting for 94.9% of total exports, including eight products that exceeded $10 billion, which made up 73.4%. Processing products dominated exports at $452.74 billion, or 90.7%, followed by agricultural and forestry products at $33.48 billion (6.7%), seafood at $10.36 billion (2.1%), and fuels and minerals at $2.66 billion (0.5%). Imports in the first 10 months were worth $511.31 billion. Production materials accounted for $481.03 billion, or 94.1%, while consumer goods made up the remaining 5.9%. Vietnam posted trade surpluses of $40.84 billion with the EU and $3.42 billion with Japan, up 26.8% and 110.4% from a year ago, respectively. Meanwhile, it recorded deficits of $134.94 billion with China, $48.63 billion with South Korea and $16.93 billion with ASEAN. The Ministry of Industry and Trade plans to accelerate exports, diversify markets and improve compliance capacity, focusing on making better use of signed free trade agreements, expanding into new markets, and strengthening early warnings of trade defence cases, tariff barriers, green standards, traceability and rules of origin. It will also support businesses in improving product quality, developing brands and ensuring supply chain transparency, while promoting official export channels, expanding agricultural quarantine agreements, investing in cold-chain logistics infrastructure, and standardizing growing areas and packing facilities to meet partner markets' requirements.

기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 내년부터 중고 휴대전화와 컴퓨터, 카메라, 모니터 등 중고 전자제품과 전자부품의 수입을 금지한다. 베트남 과학기술부는 최근 수입이 금지되는 중고 전자제품 목록을 담은 시행규칙 제63/2026/TT-BKHCN호를 공포했다. 새로운 법령에는 HS코드별 수입금지 품목 목록이 담겼으며, 부품 교체를 통해 신제품 수준의 품질을 갖춘 리퍼비시 제품 역시 해당 코드에 포함되면 수입이 금지된다. 구체적으로, 이번 시행규칙은 중고 디지털 기술·전자제품 가운데 수입을 금지하는 품목 목록을 정하고 있으며, 목록은 HS 코드에 따라 전자, 정보기술, 통신 장비를 폭넓게 포함한다. 시행일은 2027년 1월 1일이다. 시행규칙 부록에 따르면 금지 품목에는 HS8470과 8471에 분류되는 중고 컴퓨터, 자동 데이터 처리 장치, 그 기능 단위 장치들이 포함된다. . 또한 HS8517에 해당하는 스마트폰과 휴대전화, 유무선 망으로 음성·영상·데이터를 주고받는 기기도 수입 금지 품목에 포함된다. 이 밖에도 △마이크 △스피커 △헤드폰 △오디오앰프 △디지털카메라 △비디오카메라 △TV카메라 △무선송수신 장비 △레이더시스템 △내비게이션기기 △무선원격제어 장비도 금지 대상이다. 모니터와 프로젝터, TV 수신 장비 등 일부 전자기기도 각자의 HS코드에 따라 포함되며, 금지 목록 제품의 중고 부품과 액세서리, 조립부품, 전자부품도 수입 금지 대상 품목이다. 특히, 수리나 부품 교체를 통해 기능과 품질, 외관이 신제품과 동일한 수준인 리퍼비시 제품도 HS코드상 수입 금지 품목에 포함되면 수입이 금지된다. 부품을 교체하고 외관을 새로 단장하고 보증까지 제공한다 해도, 해당 HS코드 분류에 속하는 중고 휴대전화나 컴퓨터는 수입이 금지된다는 의미다. 다만, 모든 중고 전자장비가 금지되는 것은 아니다. 컬러 디지털 모델을 포함한 일부 프린터와 복사기, 그리고 A0 용지를 처리하거나 분당 A4 35장 이상 인쇄·복사할 수 있는 일부 흑백 장치는 수입금지 대상 품목에서 제외되며, 반도체 제조·패키징·테스트 사업과 디지털 기술 교육·연구개발 활동에 직접 쓰이는 중고 생산 라인, 기계, 설비도 관련 법적 요건을 충족하면 수입이 허용된다. 시행일 전 관할 당국의 수입 승인을 받은 물품은 승인 문서에 정해진 조건과 유효 기간에 따라 지속적인 수입이 허용된다.

picked.t: Fansipan festival to showcase nearly 70 succulent varieties
picked.body: The Fansipan Succulent Festival 2026 will take place at Sun World Fansipan Legend in Sa Pa, northern Vietnam, showcasing nearly 70 succulent varieties and a range of visitor activities. Held at An Nhien Garden near the Fansipan cable car departure station, the nine-day event will be the festival's third edition since its launch in 2024. Under the theme "Bloom in Serenity," this year's festival is expected to be its largest, with hundreds of thousands of plants arranged in themed displays across the garden. The collection will include nearly 70 varieties, among them Sa Pa green succulent, String of Pearls, String of Nickels, Butterfly succulent, Cabbage succulent, Pink Rose succulent, Dollar Plant, Pipe succulent, Imperial succulent and Snow succulent. Nearly 10 new varieties will be introduced, including Marble succulent, Ben Badis, Butter Cream succulent, Variegated Lola, Four Directions succulent and Great Wall cactus. The plants will be displayed along the Succulent Path and throughout An Nhien Garden, with arrangements designed to complement the mountain landscape. Unlike previous editions, which featured plant carpets and installations made with stone, bamboo and wood, this year's festival will include sculptural structures incorporating living plants. The theme draws on Buddhist principles of faith, aspiration and practice, which the organizers say represent the progression from developing belief and setting goals to pursuing them through consistent action. These ideas will be reflected in the exhibition areas. Visitors can also join succulent-planting activities, attend workshops on making succulent-shaped pastries and watch artistic performances. The festival coincides with Sa Pa's transition from autumn to winter, when cooler weather draws visitors to the northern highlands. After exploring An Nhien Garden, visitors can take the cable car to Fansipan, Vietnam's highest mountain at 3,143 meters. The summit area features Buddhist structures and viewpoints overlooking the Hoang Lien Son range. Other nearby attractions include Ban May Village, which introduces visitors to the traditions, cuisine and cultural activities of ethnic communities in Vietnam's northwest. Seasonal flower gardens feature purple salvia and buckwheat.

picked.t: Vietnam, South Korea shine amid uneven Asia-Pacific tourism recovery
picked.body: PATA’s Annual Tourism Monitor, released on Oct. 22, shows Vietnam and South Korea’s arrival numbers as of the early months of 2026 were up 14.9% year-on-year and 21.4%. Vietnam received 19.5 million foreign visitors through October, according to its National Statistics Office. South Korea’s estimated numbers had surpassed its earlier full-year record of 18.94 million by Oct. 27, its tourism ministry said, as reported by Yonhap . Both countries also exceeded pre-pandemic visitor numbers. Vietnam saw a 44.5% increase over the corresponding period in 2019, while South Korea's was 28.4% higher. Their growth stood out against an uneven regional recovery. The 44 destinations tracked by PATA welcomed 239 million international visitors, up just 2.9% year-on-year and still 3.7% below the corresponding 2019 level. Some destinations recorded declines, including Thailand, where international arrivals fell 4.9% year-on-year. PATA said the next phase of growth would depend on more than restoring visitor numbers. It urged destinations to attract visitors from a wider range of markets, encourage longer stays, and spread tourism beyond major attractions and peak seasons.
